findings.description:
ProtocolRegistry.resolveActive(bytes32) (src/apps/ProtocolRegistry.sol#273-277) uses a dangerous strict equality:
	- current.version == 0 || ! current.active (src/apps/ProtocolRegistry.sol#275)
findings.reason: Version zero is the explicit unregistered sentinel; active service lookup must reject it and inactive entries. This is not an Ether balance equality.
findings.evidence: REC-9 independent state model and boundary tests; REC-3/4 real Vault and executor tests; source inspection

findings.description:
Reentrancy in TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.schedule(bytes32,bytes32,address,uint128,uint64,uint64,bytes32,bytes32) (src/treasury/TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.sol#105-145):
	External calls:
	- budgets.reserve(budgetId,amount) (src/treasury/TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.sol#128)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- _disbursements[id] = Disbursement(budgetId,recipient,b.asset,amount,notBefore,expiresAt,civicActionHash,purposeHash,bytes32(0),State.SCHEDULED,true) (src/treasury/TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.sol#129-141)
	TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420._disbursements (src/treasury/TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.sol#37) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420._get(bytes32) (src/treasury/TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.sol#188-193)
	- TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.schedule(bytes32,bytes32,address,uint128,uint64,uint64,bytes32,bytes32) (src/treasury/TreasuryDisbursementRegistry420.sol#105-145)
findings.reason: Scheduling is Timelock-only and verifies canonical ID and absence before calling the constructor-bound concrete Budget registry. reserve is controller-only and updates accounting with no untrusted call, so it cannot reenter scheduling. A failed reserve reverts the whole disbursement creation.
findings.evidence: REC-9 independent state model and boundary tests; REC-3/4 real Vault and executor tests; source inspection

findings.description:
Reentrancy in GovernanceTimelock.execute(bytes32) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#126-143):
	External calls:
	- (ok,out) = op.target.call{value: op.value}(op.data) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#138)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- executingCivicOperation = previousOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#139)
	GovernanceTimelock.executingCivicOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#35) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- GovernanceTimelock.execute(bytes32) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#126-143)
	- GovernanceTimelock.executeCivicAction(bytes32,address,bytes) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#148-159)
	- GovernanceTimelock.executingCivicOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#35)
findings.reason: Operation.executed is set before the external call; a callback cannot replay that ID. Only the activated scheduler target gets the exact operation context, and each external action clears it. A distinct already-authorized mature operation may execute independently and restores the saved context; all nested effects roll back if the outer call fails.
findings.evidence: REC-9 nested mature context and atomic rollback tests; REC-5 real governance 62/62, including Stake safety 3/3

findings.description:
Reentrancy in GovernanceTimelock.executeCivicAction(bytes32,address,bytes) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#148-159):
	External calls:
	- (success,None) = target.call{value: msg.value}(data) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#157)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- executingCivicOperation = id (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#158)
	GovernanceTimelock.executingCivicOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#35) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- GovernanceTimelock.execute(bytes32) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#126-143)
	- GovernanceTimelock.executeCivicAction(bytes32,address,bytes) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#148-159)
	- GovernanceTimelock.executingCivicOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#35)
findings.reason: Only the activated scheduler may dispatch the exact nonzero active operation; the Governor verifies Timelock caller, queued state, both committed action hashes and total value. Before calling an external target the context is zeroed, so a callback, including a target that invokes the Governor, cannot borrow it. Restoration to the original ID is necessary to dispatch the next committed action. Nested mature operations restore zero; a failed action reverts the entire batch.
findings.evidence: REC-9 nested mature context and atomic rollback tests; REC-5 real governance 62/62, including Stake safety 3/3

findings.description:
Reentrancy in GovernanceTimelock.execute(bytes32) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#126-143):
	External calls:
	- (ok,out) = op.target.call{value: op.value}(op.data) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#138)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- executingCivicOperation = previousOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#139)
	GovernanceTimelock.executingCivicOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#35) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- GovernanceTimelock.execute(bytes32) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#126-143)
	- GovernanceTimelock.executeCivicAction(bytes32,address,bytes) (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#148-159)
	- GovernanceTimelock.executingCivicOperation (src/governance/GovernanceTimelock.sol#35)
findings.reason: Operation.executed is set before the external call; a callback cannot replay that ID. Only the activated scheduler target gets the exact operation context, and each external action clears it. A distinct already-authorized mature operation may execute independently and restores the saved context; all nested effects roll back if the outer call fails.
findings.evidence: REC-9 nested mature context and atomic rollback tests; REC-5 real governance 62/62, including Stake safety 3/3

Before calling an external target the context is zeroed, so a callback, including a target that invokes the Governor, cannot borrow it. Restoration to the original ID is necessary to dispatch the next committed action. Nested mature operations restore zero; a failed action reverts the entire batch.
